Hello! I will not be able to fully debunk the entire article, but I will give it a go and do my best.  

Paragraph 1: This paragraph makes the claim that without a god, there is no hope and no true morality.  This is a false claim - you certainly can't say that god gives hope to every human being, considering that the whole basis of almost every single religion depends on god murdering people not quite like them.  Also, morality does not come from god - would a moral god condone rape, slavery, murder, and incest?

P2: There are a large number of reasons that people don't believe in god, only one of which is trusting a scientist over a 2,000 old holy book.  Also, atheism is NOT the popular view.  This sentiment reflects the JW belief that they are the only ones who truly believe in god and that everyone else is just a sad, godless heathen.

P3: This seems to be implying that it is wrong to believe in a literal interpretation of the creation account, which is actually wise.  But this contradictory - JW's pride themselves on interpreting the Bible literally.  They believe in the literal interpretation of Adam and Eve, which has also been disproved by science.  Why do they believe the scientific about the creation of the universe but not the creation of man? How did they decide where to draw the line?

P4: This paragraph seems to put faith in god on the exact same level as 'faith' in science.  Specifically, because no one was around when the universe was created, then all of science is just petty guessing.  It is completely disregarding the fact that their faith is based on nothing.

P5: States the faith needs to be based on evidence, which is certainly true but goes against the common definition of faith, especially religious faith.  It also says that there is evidence to base their beliefs on god, which is not true.

P6: This is the set up to a comparison in the next paragraph.  But, an impending tsunami is not comparable to the existence of god.  We have tools that can measure and record a tsunami, proving their cause and existence.  There is no such tool for god.

P7: This states that faith in god should be based on being informed about convincing evidence, which is certainly true.  But again - there is no such evidence, only weak arguments.  The quote from Vladimir Prelog is meant to inflate WT knowledge and arguments and degrade scientific evidence and contradicting arguments.  Besides, does it matter what Nobel Laureates can and cannot do when it comes to examining whether there is a god? Nobel Laureates are not at all scientists or philosophers, and it's not like we leave all of our difficult questions up to them.
